title: Hierarchical dequant batching for attention prefill to reduce per-token dequant overhead
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: In mixed-precision streaming workloads (INT8/FP8 fallbacks) we see a non-trivial CPU and memory overhead from repeated per-token dequant conversions during prefill. This overhead increases tail latency on short-prefill-paths and amplifies cost when many small requests are served concurrently. Goal: implement a hierarchical dequant batching layer that (1) groups incoming prefill requests at multiple levels (precision-path, sequence-length bucket, head-group compatibility), (2) performs dequantization once per batch/cluster, and (3) co-schedules clustered attention kernels to amortize dequant cost while preserving latency SLOs and compatibility with KV cache reuse. This ticket covers design, prototype, perf evaluation, and a staged rollout for hosted API and Dedicated runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: p95 prefill latency improvement >= 15% on mixed-precision traces compared to baseline
no regression (>5%) in end-to-end decode latency for long-sequence workloads
automated unit+integration tests exercise cluster boundaries and KV cache correctness
feature gated and disabled by default for customers using strict single-precision profiles
end-to-end benchmark artifacts (perf dashboard + reproducible harness) published
implementation_steps: Design: define clustering keys (precision-path, seq-length bucket, per-head compatibility mask) and cost model for when to form a cluster vs run immediately
Runtime: add DequantClusterer module in serving runtime that's invoked in prefill path before kernel selection
KV integration: ensure clustered prefill writes to shared KV buffer with correct token offsets and reference counting
Kernel changes: add small kernel adapter to accept pre-dequantized buffers or perform zero-copy reinterpret when supported
Fallbacks: implement strict timeout (e.g., 0.8 * latency_budget) where unclustered requests are flushed immediately to meet SLO
Tests: unit tests for boundary conditions, fuzz tests for mixed precision signatures, end-to-end harness against sampled production traces
Perf: run microbench suite on p4d and a100 equivalent, gather p50/p95/p99, GPU util, and CPU overhead
Rollout: staged canary on hosted API (10% traffic) -> 50% -> full; Dedicated opt-in via runtime flag; validate telemetry and kill-switch
risks: Clustering can add extra queuing latency for isolated low-volume requests if thresholds are mis-tuned
Interaction with KV cache offsets might introduce subtle correctness bugs for concurrent write/merge semantics
Memory overhead for temporary FP32/FP16 scratch buffers could increase GPU memory pressure and reduce model batch sizes
Hardware variability: INT8/FP8 fastpaths differ across vendors and may require per-backend tuning
Observability gaps: need to ensure per-cluster telemetry to diagnose misgrouping and cost attribution
perf_targets: prefill p95 reduced by >=15% (mixed precision workloads)
token throughput improvement >=10% for <128 token prefills on INT8 paths
CPU dequant cycles reduced by >=40% for clustered traffic patterns
no more than 5% memory overhead increase in worst-case clustered buffers
experiment_plan: Local prototype: synthetic workload generator that emits mixed-precision prefill traces (varying seq len and head masks)
Stage 1: unit perf on single-GPU with isolated requests to validate no regressions
Stage 2: scaled perf on multi-GPU sim to measure GPU/CPU balance and memory impact
Stage 3: canary on hosted API with shadow traffic for Dedicated customers, collect telemetry for 48 hours
Stage 4: gradual rollout with automated rollback if cluster_hit_ratio < 0.6 or p95 regresses >10%
